But the mechanism claim is false, and the mechanism was carrying the whole 'lean GO', because +0.87pp with worse DD sits inside the harness's own same-day vintage drift of -0.75pp. Reimplementing both scoring branches shows v3route barely reorders financials (within-block rank corr 0.74-0.86) while collapsing the block's top tail (fin P90 0.898 -> 0.651 in 2018, 0.829 -> 0.645 in 2022; financials in the pool top-60 go 6 -> 0), with non-financial P90 untouched. The cause is that value_score_v2 mixes an ABSOLUTE pb_z transform (max 1.0 only at pb_z <= -1) into a cross-route cut where everything else is pure-percentile and always contains 1.0s. 'Verbatim rating_8l' is the cause rather than the defence: rating_8l only ever scores within a route, so its calibration was never required to be cross-route comparable, and all 6 selfchecks are within-route or byte-identity so none could catch it. This also resolves the killer objection in the worst way — 2026 is the one quarter where the financial tail recovers (pb_z coverage now 93-96%), which is exactly the era the edge turns negative, so the recent underperformance is an artifact decaying as the data improves, not noise. The user's premise (a bank's PCF is deposit/loan flow and does not belong on a manufacturer's ruler) is correct and worth pursuing; v3route just confounds it with a scale defect.
